newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Gasunie to sell gas to Poland over 15 years. [CORRECTED 19:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dutch Gasunie to sell gas to Poland over 15 years. [CORRECTED 19:12 GMT]

text.p: Dutch gas distributor Gasunie said on Thursday it had signed a letter of intent with the Polish Oil and Gas Company (POGC) for sales of natural gas over 15 years from the Netherlands to Poland.
The letter of intent was signed on Thursday in Warsaw and the parties expect to reach a final agreement this year on the sales of about two billion cubic metres per year.

Gasunie did not give financial details, but spokesman Abraham Warner suggested Gasunie would earn around five billion guilders ($2.6 billion) from the deal (corrects earnings estimate from from 16 billion guilders).
"We sold 90 billion cubic metres to the Germans (Ruhrgas) for 15 billion guilders (corrects from 50 billion guilders). So it should be about a third of that," he said.

The letter of intent also involves an agreement to cooperate in marketing activities so as to increase gas use by households and utilities as well as promoting environmentally friendly use among industries, Gasunie said.
"POGC and Gasunie will study in the next months the possibilities for market-development supported by know-how and experiences derived from the Dutch gas market," Gasunie said in a statement.
Gasunie is 50 percent owned by the Dutch state and 25 percent each by Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon Corp unit Esso.
